content:
You are an expert scheduling formalizer.

Translate each natural-language async planning problem into a JSON scheduling
specification for a CP-SAT solver.

Rules:
1. Each numbered step in the problem becomes exactly one action.
2. Use action="task" for every action.
3. Use the exact ids step1, step2, ..., stepN based on the step numbers in the
   problem text.
4. Use item values identical to the action ids: step1, step2, ..., stepN.
5. Duration must be the integer number of seconds for that step.
6. Add a dependency only when the problem states that one step must happen
   before another. Do not add extra dependencies.
7. Do not add stations, robots, or resources.
8. Output only valid JSON in this exact shape:
{
  "actions": [
    {"id": "step1", "action": "task", "item": "step1", "duration": 120},
    {"id": "step2", "action": "task", "item": "step2", "duration": 300}
  ],
  "dependencies": [
    {"before": "step1", "after": "step2"}
  ]
}
9. Before finishing, verify that:
   - every step from 1..N appears exactly once in actions
   - every dependency endpoint is an existing action id
   - durations are integer seconds
   - there are no duplicate actions

Problem:
To splint a dog's leg, here are the steps needed.
Step 1. Sterilize the wound site (5 minutes)
Step 2. Apply final protective outer layer (10 minutes)
Step 3. Layer soft cast padding (8 minutes)
Step 4. Measure the length of the limb (2 minutes)
Step 5. Gather wooden tongue depressors for stabilization (1 minute)
Step 6. Cut the medical tape into strips (3 minutes)
Step 7. Secure the padding with initial tape (2 minutes)
Step 8. Roll out the primary bandage layer (4 minutes)
Step 9. Position the leg in a neutral standing angle (3 minutes)
Step 10. Check for proper blood flow in the toes (1 minute)
Step 11. Apply antiseptic cream (2 minutes)
Step 12. Adjust the dog's collar to prevent biting (2 minutes)
Step 13. Prepare the splint material (6 minutes)
Step 14. Wash your hands thoroughly (3 minutes)
Step 15. Put on sterile gloves (1 minute)
Step 16. Organize the workspace (5 minutes)
Step 17. Calm the dog with a treat (2 minutes)
Step 18. Place the dog on a stable table (4 minutes)
Step 19. Retrieve a muzzle for safety (1 minute)
Step 20. Wrap the secondary compression layer (7 minutes)
Step 21. Inspect the skin for irritation (4 minutes)
Step 22. Clear the area of debris (3 minutes)
Step 23. Dispose of used packaging (1 minute)
Step 24. Apply a topical numbing agent (10 minutes)
Step 25. Check the splint for tightness (2 minutes)
Step 26. Log the procedure in medical notes (5 minutes)
Step 27. Have an assistant hold the dog's head (10 minutes)
Step 28. Double-check the alignment (2 minutes)
Step 29. Mark the splint cutting line (1 minute)
Step 30. Align the splint along the bone (4 minutes)
Step 31. Verify the joint is immobilized (2 minutes)
Step 32. Trim the excess splint material (5 minutes)
Step 33. Sharpen the cutting shears (10 minutes)
Step 34. Check the dog's temperature (3 minutes)
Step 35. Shave the fur around the injury (15 minutes)
Step 36. Open the emergency kit (1 minute)
Step 37. Administer a mild sedative (20 minutes)
Step 38. Prepare the adhesive solvent (2 minutes)
Step 39. Apply a non-stick pad to the wound (2 minutes)
Step 40. Clean the splint surface (3 minutes)
Step 41. Verify the dog's weight for medication (5 minutes)
Step 42. Lay out a clean towel (1 minute)
Step 43. Call the veterinarian for advice (10 minutes)
Step 44. Position the stirrups (4 minutes)
Step 45. Smooth out any wrinkles in the wrap (3 minutes)
Step 46. Apply an antibiotic spray (1 minute)
Step 47. Check the dog's breathing rate (2 minutes)
Step 48. Set a timer for the setting agent (1 minute)
Step 49. Clean the leg with saline solution (6 minutes)
Step 50. Locate the first aid manual (2 minutes)
Step 51. Assess the severity of the fracture (5 minutes)
Step 52. Lay out the gauze rolls (2 minutes)
Step 53. Wrap the cotton undercast (6 minutes)
Step 54. Prepare a bowl of warm water (4 minutes)
Step 55. Select the correct splint size (2 minutes)
Step 56. Check the dog's heart rate (2 minutes)
Step 57. Calm the owner (10 minutes)
Step 58. Secure the distal end of the splint (3 minutes)
Step 59. Plug in the exam light (1 minute)
Step 60. Sanitize the examination area (15 minutes)
Step 61. Remove the cap from the adhesive (1 minute)
Step 62. Prepare a recovery crate (10 minutes)
Step 63. Fetch the scissors (2 minutes)
Step 64. Check the expiration date on the bandages (1 minute)
Step 65. Apply the lateral support bars (5 minutes)
Step 66. Soak the fiberglass material (3 minutes)
Step 67. Palpate the leg for swelling (4 minutes)
Step 68. Read the instructions on the splint kit (5 minutes)
Step 69. Stabilize the joint above the injury (5 minutes)
Step 70. Monitor the dog for shock (15 minutes)
